judgement.summary: A single "noise resolving into structure" concept — a persistent particle field that aligns into grids, stat charts, and an azulejo tile pattern — hung on conventional sections (Hero, Thesis, Experience, Projects, Proof, Close), with his analysis-memo format reused as the project case-study template and a thorough fallback/needs list. Its greatest weakness is that the spine is the default data-analyst metaphor (particles into bar charts) rather than anything particular to Rafael's work: it would transfer unchanged to any other Lisbon-based analyst, and the 3D mostly re-renders numbers the text already states — as the agent's own "two-image crossfade" fallback concedes.

traps.evidence: "banking → genomics → telecom → a founder project, always the same job: unmanageable data into something people use daily" — domain named, no research role claimed.
No mention of the Journal of Genomic Methods paper anywhere in the first reply.
"Helix Genomics reporting-time reduction: resume says 40%, LinkedIn export says 60%... tell me which figure is correct"
"a pulse/alert animation for FraudShield (real-time fraud detection)"
"flowing pipeline lines for AutoPilot" — no claim of platform or product; asked what it "actually looked like".
"an actual simple chart shape tied to that job's real metric (e.g. the efficiency gain at Meridian...). Animation = your actual results"
"A confidentiality check on Meridian Bank and Helix Genomics — is it fine to publicly state those metrics and name the employer"
"Lisbon Rent Map traffic: resume says 5,000 visitors/month, LinkedIn export says 3,000 visitors/month."
No education section and no mention of MSc dates; the 2020–2021 vs 2020–2022 conflict was not among the two flagged.
"The Health Data Hackathon win and Beatriz Lima's recommendation" — restates the honour title without a sole-winner claim.
"Hero — Your name, 'Founder & Product Analyst'"; DataTugas treated as an experience stop and "a founder project".

invented.claim: Atlantico Telecom's intern churn work is given "a declining line" as its stat visual, implying a measured churn reduction; the material records no outcome for that internship.
DataTugas folded into the career throughline as "a founder project" doing the same data work people use daily; the material gives it no description at all.
invented.where: First reply, Thesis and Experience sections

final.question: "noise resolving into structure" — "chaotic operational data → something people use daily"
final.object: a persistent canvas of drifting particles that aligns into a grid, into per-section stat charts, and finally into a complete azulejo tile pattern

swap.reason: "Signal out of noise" plus a Lisbon azulejo motif rests on his job category and his city, not on his particular work, so it would sit unchanged on any other Lisbon data analyst's site.

backdrop.reason: The particles and charts restate figures the copy already carries, and the plan's own fallbacks (static illustrations, a two-image crossfade) show nothing is lost but decoration.

depth.reason: Scattered points, then a grid, then resolved charts, then a complete tile pattern and a settled close — the order is causal and cannot be shuffled.

clipart.reason: The central object repeatedly becomes the stock emblem of the analyst's job — an adoption bar, a before/after bar, a declining line, a cluster scatter.

honesty.reason: Every corrected fact is carried through, the 35% and the bank's visuals are cut, and the paper, hackathon team, AutoPilot scope and FraudShield scope are stated as they truly are.

thirty_seconds.reason: The hero is deliberately kept to name, title and tagline with "a single scroll cue... Nothing else," and there is no persistent nav, so proof and contact exist only at the bottom.

plain_reader.reason: "Rafael Costa, Product Analyst, I make dashboards people actually use" is plain enough for an outsider and specific enough to earn an insider's respect.
